title: Standing Instruction of the Premium Accounting Office: Billing the Ridgecrest Advantage Plan Premium
content:
The plan bills the monthly plan premium of the Ridgecrest Advantage Medicare Advantage Health Plan held for each coverage month from the coverage effective date to the coverage end date, and the charge falls due on the premium due day of that coverage month. The amount of the charge for a coverage month is the monthly plan premium of the plan held.

**Condition of record.** The enrollment is in a status of coverage in force or coverage in its premium grace period on the day the charge is posted. The enrollment record is the authority, tested before the charge is posted and matched on the enrollment reference.

**Cadence.** A quarterly billing frequency bills three coverage months in one charge posted in the first of those months; what the member owes for a coverage month never changes with the frequency.

**The low-income premium subsidy.** Where the member qualifies for the low income premium subsidy the full premium is still charged and the subsidy is posted separately as a credit adjustment, so the amount owed is always the charge less the credits posted against it.

**The Part B premium reduction.** The Part B premium reduction the plan carries is never billed or credited here: Social Security applies it to the member's Part B premium, and it never appears on the plan premium account.

**Months after coverage ends.** No premium is charged for a coverage month beginning after the coverage end date, and a charge already posted for such a month is relieved by a credit adjustment rather than left outstanding.

### Basis questions

**A member on a quarterly cadence asks why one charge is so much larger than the monthly premium.** One quarterly charge carries three coverage months, posted in the first of those months. What is owed for any one of those coverage months is the same monthly plan premium as it would be on a monthly cadence.

**A member awarded the low income premium subsidy asks why the full premium still appears as a charge.** The full premium is still charged, and the subsidy reaches the account as a separate credit adjustment. The amount owed is the charge less the credits posted against it.

**A member on Ridgecrest Advantage Essential (HMO) asks why the Part B premium reduction does not show on their premium account.** It never appears there. Social Security applies it to the member's Part B premium instead.
